Additionally, studies have shown that people from <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups">underrepresented groups</a> are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#equal-employment-opportunity-policy" target="_blank">GitLab’s EEO Policy</a> and <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/labor-and-employment-notices/#eeoc-us-equal-employment-opportunity-commission-notices" target="_blank">EEO is the Law</a>. If you have a disability or special need that requires <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#reasonable-accommodation" target="_blank">accommodation</a>, please let us know during the <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/interviewing/#adjustments-to-our-interview-process" target="_blank">recruiting process</a>.</p></div>

issues, merge requests, and the GitLab handbook.</li> </ul> <h4>What you’ll bring</h4> <ul> <li value="1"><span class="textBold">Experience leading</span> engineering organizations with multiple teams and managers in a distributed environment.</li> <li value="2"><span class="textBold">Strong understanding of</span> application security fundamentals, including Static Application Security Testing, Software Composition Analysis, secret detection, vulnerability management workflows, and software supply chain security.</li> <li value="3"><span class="textBold">Experience building</span> detection, analysis, or scanning systems in a software as a service or DevSecOps environment, including trade-offs across precision, recall, latency, and scale.</li> <li value="4"><span class="textBold">Direct experience shipping</span> a customer-facing AI or machine learning product feature tied to detection or remediation quality outcomes.</li> <li value="5"><span class="textBold">Ability to title: Director, Strategic Partnerships
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An overview of this role</strong></p> <p>As the Director, Strategic Partnerships, you will own two of GitLab's most important external relationships. This is a single-threaded owner role within the Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships. You will shape partnership strategy from the top down and drive execution from the ground up — this is as much about running the weekly grind of a partnership as it is about setting its direction, turning strategic relationships into durable business outcomes.</p> <p>This role sits close to GitLab's evolving AI strategy and the future of our AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You will help define where technical integration, commercial alignment, and joint go-to-market efforts can create the most value for GitLab. You will develop a clear point of view, represent these partnerships with senior stakeholders, and personally drive the day-to-day work that spans multi-year planning and weekly execution — chasing down blockers, keeping work streams on track, and doing the detailed follow-through yourself rather than delegating it.</p> <p><strong>What you'll do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary owner and point of contact for one hyperscaler and one major AI lab, personally accountable for the direction, operating rhythm, and outcomes of each partnership, including the tactical work of keeping things moving week to week.</li> <li>Develop and drive multi-year partnership strategies and joint plans that connect GitLab's business priorities, product roadmap, and AI strategy with concrete partner initiatives — and then own getting those plans executed.</li> <li>Build strong working relationships across partner organizations, including executives, product management, engineering, sales, and marketing stakeholders.</li> <li>Run a disciplined operating cadence across complex initiatives, with clear priorities, owners, timelines, coordination points, and follow-through you drive yourself.</li> <li>Coordinate cross-functional work inside GitLab to support partnership goals, aligning teams across product, engineering, sales, marketing, and the executive group.</li> <li>Translate partner opportunities and requests into actionable internal plans, including roadmap discussions, integration needs, commercial motions, and executive recommendations.</li> <li>Track and communicate measurable partnership outcomes such as pipeline influence, annual recurring revenue impact, integration progress, and joint go-to-market execution.</li> <li>Represent the partnerships at the executive level by preparing clear recommendations, briefing executives, and helping drive alignment on investments, trade-offs, and next steps.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you'll bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>Significant experience building and managing strategic partnerships, business development relationships, or alliance programs in enterprise software, cloud, and/or AI — with a track record of being in the details, not just setting direction.</li> <li>Strong ownership mindset with the ability to operate as a single-threaded owner who is accountable for both strategy and execution, and comfortable doing the hands-on work personally rather than handing it off.</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex partnership topics into clear recommendations for executives and cross-functional stakeholders.</li> <li>Strong project and program management skills, including the ability to organize complex workstreams, prioritize effectively, and keep multiple initiatives moving through direct, hands-on management.</li> <li>Technical fluency in software development, platform integrations, and the AI or machine learning landscape, with comfort engaging engineering and product counterparts in substantive conversations.</li> <li>Experience working with senior stakeholders on high-visibility initiatives, including preparing executive briefings, framing recommendations, and driving follow-through.</li> <li>Ability to influence without formal authority, build strong working relationships across internal and external teams, and navigate multiple priorities with sound judgment.</li> <li>Familiarity with the DevSecOps ecosystem and a results-oriented approach to measuring partnership impact through business and product outcomes.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Strategic Partnerships team owns the strategy and relationship management for some of GitLab's most consequential external partners, including hyperscalers and AI companies that are shaping the future of software development. We work across product, engineering, sales, marketing, and the executive group to turn partnerships into differentiated growth for GitLab and to ensure those relationships support our long-term platform strategy.</p> <p>We play an especially important role as GitLab continues to expand its AI-powered DevSecOps vision. relationships and practical knowledge needed to navigate partner-led deals and help move opportunities across the finish line.</li> <li value="13">Manage one-to-many partner engagement through partner portals and automated systems, providing weekly pipeline forecasts, partner-sourced opportunity reports, and clear insights into campaign performance and territory impact.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Experience in sales development, business development, channel sales, or partner-driven pipeline generation in a business-to-business environment.</li> <li value="2">Experience working with US public sector channel strategy across federal, state, local, or education markets.</li> <li value="3">Practical knowledge of government procurement and contract vehicles, such as General Services Administration schedules, Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement, and National Association of State Procurement Officials agreements.</li> <li value="4">Familiarity with partner ecosystems, including programmatic engagement and demand generation with distributors, long-tail partners, and hyperscalers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud.</li> <li value="5">Ability to design, execute, and improve scalable, campaign-driven demand generation, including one-to-many partner engagement and event-driven campaigns.</li> <li value="6">Experience using Salesforce and modern sales development or marketing automation tools to manage, forecast, and report on partner-sourced pipeline and campaign performance.</li> <li value="7">Strong analytical skills to interpret campaign results, partner activation metrics, and territory impact, then turn those insights into clear plans.</li> <li value="8">Effective written and verbal communication skills, with a focus on repeatable messaging and collaboration with Account Executives, Field Marketing, and regional sales leadership.</li> <li value="9">Interest in GitLab, open source software, and modern software development practices, with the ability to learn and use GitLab and related tools.</li> <li value="10">Openness to travel for partner events and field collaboration and to apply transferable skills from related sales, partner, or digital marketing roles in a remote, results-focused environment.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Ecosystem Sales team builds and scales a high-impact partner network that drives Scale growth through partner-sourced pipeline and new logo acquisition. You'll own enablement content for our AI capabilities and Duo Agent Platform (DAP), along with the program initiatives that support the field across onboarding, product education, release readiness, revenue plays, and ongoing reinforcement. The overall aim of the role is to ensure field teams can clearly explain value throughout the customer buying lifecycle.</p> <p>You'll work across Product Marketing, Product Management, Revenue Operations, Solutions Architecture, Customer Success, Monetization, and Field Leadership to bring new offerings, product updates, and messaging to market through clear, role-based enablement. In this individual contributor role, you'll use instructional design, strong program management, and performance insights to create learning experiences that are practical, accessible, and easy for the field to use in the flow of work. You'll do this in GitLab's all-remote, asynchronous environment, where autonomy, collaboration, and iteration are part of how we work.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li>Designing and launching role-based learning paths, certifications, and technical labs that help account executives, solutions architects, customer success managers, and partners build skill in GitLab's AI capabilities and DAP</li> <li>Building and maintaining enablement content for product launches, new offers, and monthly release readiness, including talk tracks, demo guidance, competitive positioning, and field-ready assets</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the strategy and roadmap for Field Enablement Content programs focused on GitLab's AI-powered platform story, aligned to the needs of customer-facing teams.</li> <li>Lead cross-functional enablement programs for product launches, new offerings, packaging changes, and release readiness from planning through launch, reinforcement, and ongoing updates.</li> <li>Build and maintain role-based enablement assets such as playbooks, talk tracks, pitch materials, demo flows, technical labs, and assessments that help the field communicate value clearly.</li> <li>Design blended learning experiences, including self-paced content, live virtual sessions, scenario-based learning, and hands-on practice, for field and partner audiences.</li> <li>Develop and manage accreditations, certifications, and validation programs that help teams build and demonstrate readiness across priority solution areas.</li> <li>Partner with Product Marketing, Product Management, Solutions Architecture, Revenue Operations, Customer Success, Monetization, and Enablement Leads to ensure content is accurate, current, and easy to apply in customer conversations.</li> <li>Publish and organize content in Google Drive and using AI tools so that materials are discoverable, structured, and aligned to role-based learning paths and business priorities.</li> <li>Measure program effectiveness through engagement, completion, assessment, and field feedback data, and continuously improve content governance, review cycles, and program quality over time.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Demonstrated experience in sales enablement, technical enablement, learning and development, product marketing, solutions architecture, or a related role supporting B2B enterprise software go-to-market teams.</li> <li>Experience creating and delivering enablement for customer-facing audiences such as account executives, solutions architects, customer success managers, or partners, including content that supports real customer conversations.</li> <li>Familiarity with DevSecOps and AI concepts, with the ability to turn technical topics into clear, value-based messaging for field teams.</li> <li>Strong instructional design skills and experience building scalable learning programs using adult learning principles and structured methods such as ADDIE, SAM, or similar approaches.</li> <li>Proven ability to manage complex, cross-functional programs with multiple stakeholders, timelines, and dependencies while maintaining a high bar for quality and clarity.</li> <li>Experience creating a range of enablement materials such as e-learning modules, presentations, guides, demos, labs, assessments, and reinforcement content.</li> <li>Comfort using content management, enablement and learning platforms, along with common collaboration and content creation tools.</li> <li>A data-informed mindset, strong written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to work as a self-directed manager of one in an all-remote, asynchronous, values-driven environment.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Our <strong>Field Enablement & GTM AI </strong>team helps GitLab's revenue organization build the knowledge, skills, and behaviors needed to support customer outcomes and revenue growth. We create scalable programs, content, and processes that help our field and partner teams stay ready for product launches, new offers, evolving messaging, and ongoing skills development across the customer journey.</p> <p>You'll join our team and work closely with stakeholders across the business to connect product change with field readiness. We focus on making enablement practical, measurable, and easy to use, with an emphasis on role-based learning, clear content governance, and repeatable frameworks that can scale globally. We're a collaborative, fully remote team that values transparency, iteration, and shared ownership as we build programs that help GitLab teams tell a stronger, more consistent story in the market.</p> <h4><strong>How GitLab will support you</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/" target="_blank">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/paid-time-off/" target="_blank">Flexible Paid Time Off</a> </li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/erg-guide/#:~:text=Definition%20of%20the%20TMRG%20%2D%20Team%20Member%20Resource%20Groups,-TMRGs%20are%20voluntary&text=The%20purpose%20for%20this%20type,developing%20the%20sense%20of%20belonging." target="_blank">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/" target="_blank">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/" target="_blank">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave" target="_blank">Parental leave</a> </li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/expenses/#equipment" target="_blank">Home office</a> support</li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. You’ll need to be comfortable going well beyond people management and into the architecture of high-throughput, multi-component data systems: ingestion, buffering, enrichment, replication, storage, querying, backpressure handling, isolation, and production operations across multiple deployment models.</p> <p>You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, Infrastructure, Data, and other Engineering teams to evolve a platform that lives inside the product, keeps external services to a minimum, and runs across GitLab.com, Dedicated, Self-Managed, and Cells-based deployments.</p> <p>In addition to Data Insights Platform, this role will take on classic search scope as the team joins the Data Foundations organization. You’ll help lead architecture and execution across both GitLab’s analytics platform and classic search capabilities, balancing platform depth with customer-facing impact.</p> <p>You’ll help lead architecture and execution across both GitLab’s analytics platform and classic search capabilities, balancing platform depth with customer-facing impact.</p> <p>In this role, you’ll balance technical guidance with people management. You’ll hire, coach, and develop engineers while also helping drive architecture and execution across a platform built around stateless ingesters, Siphon CDC replication, NATS/JetStream buffering, enrichment pipelines, ClickHouse-backed storage, and a Query API that interfaces with the GitLab Rails monolith.</p> <p>In Data Foundations, we build the engineering systems that make platform data reliable, scalable, and available to product teams across GitLab, and you’ll help guide that work.</p> <h4><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li> <p>Hire, manage, and enable a high-performing Data Insights Platform engineering team, creating an environment where team members can do their best work and deliver strong results.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner closely with product managers, product designers, and peer engineering managers to define and deliver the roadmap for <a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/analytics-section/platform-insights/core/">Data Insights Platform</a> (DIP) and related Platform Insights initiatives such as <a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/analytics-section/siphonhttps://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/analytics-section/siphon">Siphon</a>, Query API integrations, classic search initiatives, and self-service reporting foundations.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own delivery for your team, including planning, prioritization, execution, and operational follow-through across architecture work, platform improvements, and production readiness, with clear accountability for roadmap milestones and delivery outcomes.</p> </li> <li> <p>Guide the technical design of distributed data-path components, including ingestion, buffering, enrichment, exporting, and querying, and shape architecture choices on sharding, partitioning, component-specific scaling, failure recovery, and tenant isolation across SaaS, Dedicated, self-managed, and Cells deployments, with a strong focus on reliability, throughput, operability, and maintainability.</p> </li> <li> <p>Help the team design safe and scalable integrations with the GitLab monolith, including gRPC/Protobuf-based query paths and clear ownership boundaries between DIP and product teams building user-facing GraphQL or REST endpoints.</p> </li> <li> <p>Drive a high bar for security, privacy, and governance in how platform data is handled, including authentication, authorization, encryption, and safe handling of data with different privacy classifications.</p> </li> <li> <p>Improve operational maturity across the platform, including observability, metrics, logging, readiness, capacity planning, performance monitoring, and clear runbooks for managed environments, with a focus on improving availability, throughput, latency, and time to recovery.</p> </li> <li> <p>Collaborate asynchronously across teams and functions to help GitLab land customer-facing reporting capabilities on top of a strong, scalable data foundation.</p> </li> <li> <p>Lead the design and evolution of the platform with a focus on modular architecture, ensuring systems are extensible and ready for AI-driven integrations.</p> </li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li> <p>Experience managing platform, infrastructure, or data systems teams at scale, with a track record of building high-performing, values-aligned teams.</p> </li> <li> <p>Deep distributed systems expertise, including strong judgment on service boundaries, asynchronous pipelines, backpressure, fault tolerance, horizontal scalability, and operating multi-component systems in production.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong technical background in backend and platform engineering, with the ability to guide architecture for high-throughput event pipelines and data systems.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with technologies and patterns relevant to this space, such as change data capture, event streaming or messaging systems, OLAP data stores, query-serving layers, and service-to-service APIs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Ability to hire, develop, and coach team members while still contributing technical guidance on complex architecture and delivery tradeoffs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, especially when ownership is split between platform teams and feature teams consuming common infrastructure or APIs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience building or operating systems across multiple deployment models, with sound judgment about the tradeoffs between GitLab.com, Dedicated, self-managed, and cell-based environments.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong written communication skills and the ability to work effectively in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</p> </li> <li> <p>Familiarity with search, indexing, and query-serving systems is a strong plus.</p> </li> <li> <p>A deep passion for reliability, customer outcomes, and engineering and operational excellence, with a proven track record of instilling these values in high-performing teams.</p> </li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>In Data Foundations, we enable customers to self-serve reporting with scalable architecture. Our vision is to build a comprehensive dashboards-as-a-service framework that uses AI and relies on scalable data infrastructure.</p> <p>Data Insights Platform is one of our central initiatives, and we play a key role in advancing self-service reporting across GitLab. This is the foundational layer every reporting and intelligence surface at GitLab depends on — from product dashboards to Software Engineering Intelligence to the GitLab Knowledge Graph.</p> <p>In addition to Data Insights Platform, the team’s scope will include classic search as part of the broader Data Foundations organization.This brings together foundational analytics and search capabilities that help customers generate insights from product data and find relevant information across GitLab.</p> <p>We partner closely with product teams to turn DIP’s real-time insights, Postgres-to-ClickHouse replication, event routing, and downstream exports into dashboards, agent experiences, and customer-facing reporting.</p> <p>The scale expectations are real: we handle very large event volumes, with current and projected usage in the hundreds of millions of events per day.</p> <p>For more on how we work, see:</p> <ul> <li> <p><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/analytics/platform-insights/">Platform Insights Group</a></p> </li> <li> <p><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/architecture/design-documents/data_insights_platform/">Data Insights Platform architecture blueprint</a></p> </li> <li> <p><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/architecture/design-documents/data_insights_platform_querying_api/">Data Insights Platform Querying API</a></p> </li> </ul><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. Growth teams work iteratively, operate across product areas, and use experimentation to make data-informed product choices.</p> <p>In this role, you’ll balance technical guidance with people management. You’ll guide architecture and implementation discussions, help the team navigate tradeoffs, and ensure experiments and product changes are built carefully, measured well, and aligned with long-term product ownership. Because Growth often works across product boundaries, you’ll also help your team work effectively with counterpart groups and smoothly hand off or scale successful work where ongoing ownership belongs elsewhere.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Improving signup, onboarding, and activation experiences to help new users get to value faster</p> </li> <li> <p>Running experiments and A/B tests on GitLab.com to improve discoverability, conversion, engagement, and upgrade flows</p> </li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li> <p>Hire, guide, and enable a high-performing Growth engineering team, creating an environment where GitLab team members can do their best work and deliver strong results.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner closely with Product Managers, Product Designers, Data counterparts, and other Engineering Managers to define and deliver improvements that increase user discovery, activation, and expansion of value in GitLab.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own delivery for your team, including planning, prioritization, and execution of work across experiments and product improvements, turning learnings into measurable gains in conversion, engagement, and upgrade flows.</p> </li> <li> <p>Drive Growth’s operating model by guiding experiment ideation, ICE-based prioritization, hypothesis development, and review of results so the team can scale winning changes and stop low-impact work quickly.</p> </li> <li> <p>Guide the technical design and implementation of experiments and growth-oriented product changes, ensuring they are measured well and tied to activation, conversion, and retention outcomes.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work across Growth and other stage groups when work touches areas owned by other teams, helping your team move quickly while maintaining strong partnership and clear ownership boundaries.</p> </li> <li> <p>Dive into technical discussions and reviews, helping unblock complex issues and translating technical and experimental tradeoffs into clear context for technical and non-technical stakeholders.</p> </li> <li> <p>Foster strong async communication and healthy cross-functional operating rhythms with Product, Design, Analytics Instrumentation, Data, Customer Success, Sales, and other Growth counterparts to improve experiment execution and business outcomes.</p> </li> <li> <p>Drive the adoption of AI-native experimentation and workflows, actively identifying creative opportunities to use AI to accelerate user value delivery.</p> </li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li> <p>Experience managing product, growth, or development teams, with a track record of building high-performing, values-aligned teams.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong technical background and the ability to guide fullstack engineering work, architecture discussions, and pragmatic delivery in a product environment. Growth teams use fullstack engineering to move efficiently across frontend and backend needs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience working closely with Product, Design, and Data to deliver measurable outcomes through iteration, experimentation, and continuous improvement.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, especially in environments where work spans multiple product areas and stakeholder groups.</p> </li> <li> <p>Comfort working in a data-informed environment, including prioritizing opportunities, evaluating experiment results, and helping teams make clear, evidence-based choices.</p> </li> <li> <p>Ability to deep dive into complex technical and product issues and translate them into clear, actionable language for both technical and non-technical audiences.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience managing remote, globally distributed teams and working effectively in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with developer tools and product-led growth, and the ability to model GitLab’s values while contributing to an inclusive, high-performing culture.</p> </li> <li> <p>A demonstrated ability to challenge the status quo and creatively utilize AI-driven tools to solve complex product challenges.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Growth stage is focused on scaling GitLab’s business value by assessing the customer journey from acquisition through activation, adoption, and reactivation, and by identifying the highest-ROI levers to focus on at a given moment.</p> <p>We are a cross-functional team that works closely with Product, Design, Analytics Instrumentation, Data, Customer Success, Sales, and other product groups. Growth does not own broad product areas in the traditional sense; instead, we help users discover and unlock value throughout the GitLab application by shipping targeted improvements directly and partnering with stage groups on larger initiatives.</p> <p>Our engineering teams work with a strong experimentation mindset. This isn't a traditional field engineering, solutions architecture, or professional services role. As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work closely with customers while maintaining the technical standards and contribution discipline of a Staff-level product engineer.</p> <p>You'll work where strategic customer urgency, complex technical ambiguity, and GitLab product execution intersect. You'll partner directly with strategic customers and teams across Product, Engineering, Support, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Solutions Architecture (SA), Customer Success Architecture (CSA), Customer Success Management (CSM), and Professional Services. You'll diagnose and resolve high-impact adoption blockers, contribute production-quality fixes and features, and turn what you learn into repeatable patterns for GitLab and its customers.</p> <h2><strong>Why this role exists</strong></h2> <p>Strategic customers sometimes encounter challenges that are too broad, deep, urgent, or cross-functional for any single team to own from start to finish. These challenges may involve product gaps, performance degradation, scale bottlenecks, AI governance, adoption blockers, architectural constraints, Git usage patterns, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) complexity, application programming interface (API) automation, security requirements, or operational instability.</p> <p>Forward Deployed Engineering provides technical stewardship in these moments. The team doesn't simply observe, report, or escalate. You'll engage directly, diagnose the underlying technical problem, collaborate with the right teams, contribute code or technical solutions where appropriate, and transition the outcome into normal ownership once the customer is stable and the learning can be reused.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <h3><strong>Product contribution</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Contribute production-quality code to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.</li> <li>Develop bug fixes, features, integrations, tooling, and performance improvements when strategic customer outcomes require direct engineering work.</li> <li>Work within GitLab’s product and engineering processes, including issue discovery, merge request creation, testing, review, documentation, and maintainability.</li> <li>Partner with Product and Engineering so customer-driven solutions support long-term product direction rather than becoming one-off customizations.</li> <li>Turn blockers discovered in the field into durable product improvements, reference architectures, documentation, and repeatable implementation patterns.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Strategic technical stewardship</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Engage with strategically important customers when adoption, retention, executive confidence, or public trust is materially at risk.</li> <li>Diagnose complex problems across GitLab product behavior, customer architecture, Git internals, CI/CD workflows, API usage, observability, infrastructure, networking, and cloud environments.</li> <li>Coordinate across Product, Engineering, SRE, Support, SA, CSA, CSM, Professional Services, and customer technical teams to drive resolution from discovery through handoff.</li> <li>Provide recommendations grounded in data, traces, and systems analysis to improve GitLab usage, workflows, automation, and architecture.</li> <li>Create durable outcomes without establishing permanent dependency on Forward Deployed Engineering.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>AI adoption and agentic software development lifecycle</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Drive governed, measurable, and production-oriented adoption of GitLab Duo Agent Platform with strategic customers.</li> <li>Identify and resolve AI adoption blockers involving governance, usage controls, auditability, security, compliance, operating models, workflow design, and integrations.</li> <li>Develop customer-safe adoption patterns for the agentic software development lifecycle (SDLC), AI-assisted development, intent-based review, AI governance, and human-in-the-loop software delivery.</li> <li>Partner with Product, Engineering, Field, and Customer Success teams to turn AI adoption learning into reusable guidance and product improvements.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Thought leadership</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Create technical narratives grounded in customer experience and product reality that can help shape the industry’s approach.</li> <li>Contribute to Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, reference architectures, technical strategy memos, and adoption frameworks.</li> <li>Guide ideas through discovery, formulation, validation, amplification, and adoption across GitLab.</li> <li>Partner with SA, CSA, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Product Marketing Management, CSM, Support, and executive stakeholders to make technical thought leadership a shared company capability.</li> </ul> product codebases with high standards for testing, maintainability, performance, and security.</li> <li>Strong Ruby on Rails or Go experience and the ability to contribute directly to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.</li> <li>Experience with AI-assisted software development, agentic workflows, AI governance, model evaluation, context management, prompt and workflow design, or AI adoption in enterprise environments.</li> <li>Experience diagnosing complex system behavior across application code, data stores, infrastructure, observability, networking, APIs, and customer usage patterns.</li> Reporting to the Director of FP&A, you’ll provide timely support grounded in facts and data for critical choices. You’ll manage headcount and vendor spend, coordinate forecasting and annual planning, build financial models, explain performance, and improve the processes and tools that help make GitLab predictable.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to provide financial advice and guide direct, sometimes challenging, cross-functional conversations.</li> <li>Manage headcount planning, tracking, and reporting across supported organizations.</li> <li>Manage vendor and program spend through forecasting, analysis, and decision support.</li> <li>Coordinate monthly forecast cycles and annual planning for Product and Engineering, improving financial processes and policies with minimal guidance.</li> <li>Translate financial and data analysis into clear, evidence-based narratives, actionable insights, and recommendations that inform CFO and functional leadership decisions.</li> <li>Drive complex projects that improve data-driven decision-making and operating efficiency.</li> <li>Prioritize with limited direction and coordinate large, complex projects that improve GitLab’s ability to make evidence-based choices or operate more efficiently.</li> <li>Collaborate with cloud hosting finance, mentor finance team members, and use AI, spreadsheets, and data tools to deliver accurate, timely analysis.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience as a finance business partner supporting a business function, including headcount management, vendor spend, forecasting, variance analysis, and annual planning; This role combines deep operational governance across GitLab's AWS and GCP partnerships with the successful execution of hyperscaler operational initiatives, serving as the operational architect of the hyperscaler GTM and the primary process owner for marketplace, co-sell, and funding operations.</p> <p>You will own the technology, processes, and operational infrastructure that underpin GitLab's hyperscaler motions, serving as the go-to resource for hyperscaler partners and internal teams. This role sits at the intersection of cloud marketplace mechanics, hyperscaler funding, and systems administration, requiring someone equally comfortable setting GTM strategy, executing operationally, and leveraging AI to automate and scale hyperscaler processes.</p> <p>You will work closely with Systems, Revenue Technologies, Deal Desk, Enablement, Finance, and Legal to ensure GitLab's hyperscaler operations are accurate, scalable, and aligned to partnership objectives.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <p><strong>Marketplace Operational Strategy & Execution</strong></p> <ul> <li>Establish, oversee, and continuously improve end-to-end marketplace operational processes, including private offer management, CPPO/MCPO structures, and third-party integrations</li> <li>Serve as the internal expert on the private offer process end-to-end, partnering closely with Deal Desk to define, document, and iterate on workflows across AWS and GCP</li> <li>Own operational execution of hyperscaler funding initiatives such as AWS Strategic Collaboration Agreement (SCA), Marketplace Private Offer Partner Program (MPOPP), and GCP Marketplace Commit to Consume Program (MCCP), including milestone tracking, deal registration, claim workflows, and commit management</li> <li>Serve as the escalation point for marketplace and funding operations, resolving complex private offer, co-sell, and billing issues that span multiple systems or stakeholders</li> </ul> <p><strong>Technology Ownership & Administration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary relationship owner for the hyperscaler technology ecosystem, including Salesforce CRM partner objects, Tackle.io, and hyperscaler-specific PRM configurations</li> <li>Administer hyperscaler platforms, maintaining system health and data integrity across all hyperscaler-specific tools and integrations</li> <li>Co-manage vendor relationships, including Tackle.io and other marketplace tooling providers, covering roadmap engagement, renewal coordination, and SLA accountability</li> <li>Identify and build AI agents to automate repetitive hyperscaler workflows, such as offer status tracking, reporting, and co-sell registration, reducing manual effort and increasing operational throughput</li> <li>Partner with RevTech and Systems to maintain integration health across hyperscaler platforms, CRM, and downstream financial systems, including funding success tracking and reporting</li> </ul> <p><strong>Hyperscaler Funding Initiatives & Operational Management</strong></p> <ul> <li>Drive the operational strategy for hyperscaler funding initiatives across AWS and GCP, translating partnership objectives into co-sell and marketplace revenue plays</li> <li>Serve as the point of contact for hyperscaler partners and internal sales teams on funding operations, co-sell execution, utilization, and cross-functional escalations</li> <li>Identify opportunities to align hyperscaler funding with pipeline priorities and revenue goals</li> <li>Monitor funding performance across marketplace revenue, co-sell pipeline, and utilization; coordinate with Finance, AR, and Legal on billing and commitments</li> </ul> <p><strong>Process Design, Governance & Enablement</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, document, and govern end-to-end hyperscaler operational processes, including marketplace, co-sell, and funding initiatives, owning and maintaining the hyperscaler process map as the authoritative reference</li> <li>Continuously evaluate hyperscaler processes for AI automation opportunities, building and deploying agents that improve consistency, reduce cycle time, and scale operational capacity</li> <li>Drive gap remediation through cross-functional engagement with RSO peers and adjacent teams in IT, Finance, and Legal</li> <li>Build and maintain operational runbooks, process documentation, and training materials enabling consistent execution across all cross-functional partners</li> <li>Support configuration, testing, and maintenance of hyperscaler-facing and internal tools; document workflows and lead end-user training for field and operational teams</li> <li>Lead prioritization for hyperscaler system implementations, migrations, and platform enhancements with IT/Enterprise Applications</li> <li>Proactively surface process improvement opportunities and create GitLab Issues to advance the enhancement kickoff process</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>6+ years of experience in cloud marketplace operations with direct ownership of hyperscaler-related workflows</li> <li>Hands-on experience with Tackle.io or equivalent cloud marketplace management platforms (AWS and GCP Marketplaces)</li> <li>Working knowledge of Salesforce CRM, including partner objects, opportunity management, and basic administration</li> <li>Deep familiarity with AWS and GCP marketplace mechanics, including private offer creation, CPPO/MCPO structures, co-sell registration, and billing and disbursement workflows</li> <li>Direct experience managing hyperscaler funding initiatives such as SCA, MPOPP, and MCCP, including strategy, operational execution, and compliance requirements</li> <li>Familiarity with hyperscaler co-sell operations, including AWS ACE and GCP Partner Advantage structures and operational requirements</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to design and document complex operational processes enabling consistent execution across distributed teams</li> <li>Hands-on experience working with AI tools and building agents to automate operational workflows; comfort evaluating processes for automation potential and translating them into working solutions</li> <li>Experience serving as an operational escalation point, resolving ambiguous issues that span systems, teams, and partner relationships</li> <li>Strong cross-functional instincts; you know how to align Deal Desk, IT, Finance, Legal, and Sales stakeholders around operational changes</li> <li>Experience with B2B SaaS channel or hyperscaler funding initiatives is a must</li> <li>Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, remote-first environment with a high degree of autonomy and a bias toward action</li> </ul> <h4><strong>How GitLab will support you</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/" target="_blank">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p>GitLab features must ship successfully across four distinct deployment platforms—Self-Managed, Dedicated, Dedicated for Government, and GitLab.com. Today, developers routinely discover platform compatibility issues late in development, triggering costly rework, delays, and emergency escalations. The Platform Readiness team is building an internal developer tooling capability that embeds platform readiness intelligence directly into GitLab's software development lifecycle to solve this problem.</p> <p>As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on the newly established Platform Readiness functional team in Developer Experience, you'll contribute to the systems that enable features to ship successfully across all platforms by building and maintaining agentic workflow components and evolving the platform requirements knowledge base. This is a growth opportunity: you will learn the Platform Readiness team's agentic workflows, requirements schema, and integration surfaces from other engineers and team leadership. You'll work on concrete, high-impact problems while developing expertise in platform readiness automation and AI-driven systems.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Build and maintain agentic workflow components</strong> on the Duo Agent Platform: contribute to the Core Agentic Workflow (DAP flow) and the Requirements Agent; write tests, documentation, and evaluations for agentic-workflow behavior</li> <li><strong>Contribute to the platform requirements knowledge base</strong>: add requirements, evolve the schema, and improve validation tooling; work with platform teams to translate their expertise into structured requirements</li> <li><strong>Build integration surfaces</strong> that enable feature teams to engage the Platform Readiness team where they already work: issues, merge requests, design documents, and CI/CD pipelines</li> <li><strong>Collaborate with platform teams</strong> (Infrastructure, Security, Data) to translate their expertise into platform readiness artifacts and domain skills</li> <li><strong>Write clear and concise documentation and evaluations</strong> that validate agentic-workflow behavior and improve assessment accuracy</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <h3>Required Experience & Skills</h3> <ul> <li><strong>2+ years of software engineering experience</strong> with backend focus</li> <li><strong>Proficiency in TypeScript/Node,  Python, or Golang</strong></li> <li><strong>Comfort reading and contributing to schemas</strong> (YAML, JSON Schema) and structured content</li> <li><strong>Experience with and operational exposure to Kubernetes</strong> and reasoning about failure modes</li> <li><strong>Ability to work asynchronously</strong> and communicate clearly in written form</li> <li><strong>Exposure to and experience with LLM APIs, prompts, or agentic frameworks</strong> (does not need to be incredibly extensive)</li> </ul> <h3>Highly Valued Experience</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Ruby familiarity</strong></li> <li><strong>Experience with GitLab-style development workflows</strong> (issues, epics, merge requests, CI/CD)</li> <li><strong>Open source contributions</strong></li> <li><strong>Interest in developer experience or platform engineering</strong></li> </ul> <h3>What Makes You Stand Out (Strong Plus)</h3> <ul> <li>You have <strong>hands-on experience with any agentic workflow framework</strong> (DAP, LangGraph, etc.)</li> <li>You've <strong>contributed to a structured requirements or specification body</strong> and understand the challenges of evolving schemas</li> <li>You have <strong>observability instincts</strong> and care about measuring system behavior</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Platform Readiness team is part of GitLab Infrastructure and Developer Experience, building an internal developer tooling capability for platform readiness across GitLab's four deployment targets: Self-Managed, Dedicated, Dedicated for Government, and GitLab.com. We partner with platform teams, feature teams, and product management to ensure every feature is evaluated against platform readiness requirements before it ships.</p> <p>This is a growth opportunity where you'll learn agentic workflows, requirements schema work, and integration surface development from other engineers and team leadership. You'll contribute to high-impact work that directly improves GitLab's ability to ship features faster and more reliably across all platforms.</p> <p><br><br><br><br><br><br></p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. Working 8-hour shifts with 4 weekdays and 1 weekend day.</h4> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Support Engineering at GitLab isn’t just a title - you will be embedded within the Engineering department and will truly operate in an environment where Support and Engineering meet. You’ll interact with customers daily as they encounter the difficult edge cases of running GitLab in complex environments. In the space of a day, you might be doing behind the scenes work of a Linux administrator troubleshooting performance problems by using strace on a particular process, interacting with the Product team to ensure that steps in a bug report are reproducible, or interacting with the Engineering team itself by diving deep into our codebase and putting together a merge request to actually fix a customer issue. </span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">That’s not all though - you’d equally be invited to contribute to the source code, improve our documentation, and help build out more efficient support processes in our issue tracker. We want to live in a world where everyone can contribute, and as a member of the support team, there are no barriers to using your skills to improve the experience of our users and customers.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br></span><span style="font-weight: 400;"> Some examples of our projects: </span></p> <ul> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlab-detective">A tool to automatically check a GitLab Omnibus install for known issues</a></li> <li>A<a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlabsos"> solution to capture the state of a customer’s server</a> for easier troubleshooting</li> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/sosparser">A tool which turns log files into interactive tables to easily sort and filter columns</a></li> <li>A functionality to<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/chatops/"> ChatOps</a> to make it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">  </span></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Support a mix of Self-managed and GitLab.com (SaaS) customers and resolve their issues via Zendesk tickets, merge requests, email and video conferencing</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Collaborate with our </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/product/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Product</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/development/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Development</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Infrastructure</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-success/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Customer Success</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/sales/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Sales</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> Teams to build new features customer interactions</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Collaborate with Support team members (through </span><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-pairing/?_gl=1%2a1vj7usl%2a_ga%2aMTYyOTI0OTAxNC4xNjc4NzIwMDg0%2a_ga_ENFH3X7M5Y%2aMTY4NDgzNDU0OC4xMTAuMS4xNjg0ODM2NDM3LjAuMC4w"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Pairing Sessions</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">) and other GitLab team members (for example: as a </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/#support-stable-counterpart"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Support Stable Counterpart</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">)</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Participate in regular rotations for weekday and weekend on-call coverage (daytime only), providing emergency support to our Self-managed and SaaS customers, or working with our SaaS Production team to coordinate incident communications</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Participate in our hiring processes by reviewing applications and assessments, and by participating in interviews.</span></li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>What you’ll bring </strong></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Experience in, and passion for managing customer facing cases throughout the entire support lifecycle from initial customer inquiry to triage and reproduction, writing bug reports for hand off to the development team, and case resolution</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Excellent Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent knowledge)</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Ability to use scripting languages (preferably Ruby or Bash), and MVC frameworks (preferably Ruby on Rails)</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Experience with Git and CI/CD</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Expertise in writing support content </span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Ability to communicate complex technical topics to customers and coworkers of varying technical skill level</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Familiarity with DevOps methodologies and technologies like Serverless and Kubernetes</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Understand a range of different GitLab implementations, and how service interruptions impact the customer.</span></li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">The Support team is distributed all over the world across AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions. Support Engineers work on Support Tickets and helping GitLab’s customers, but they also dig into the code and logs to find out why something is not working as expected. The Collaboration here at GitLab is extraordinary and exciting - Support Engineers </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/workflows/how-to-get-help.html"><span style="font-weight: 400;">solve complex problems together</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and participate in regular pairing sessions and 1:1s, as well as coffee chats and Slack conversations that help them stay connected. Team members are given the ability to structure their shift the way it best suits their private life while maintaining our ability to address customer issues. </span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Thanks to our </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/all-remote/values/#transparency"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Transparency</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> value, you can see what we are working on in our </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Support Team</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> page. You’ll drive the reporting calendar, coordinate work across Accounting, Legal, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), and Investor Relations, and improve the quality, clarity, and consistency of our disclosures and reporting processes. and external reporting packages, and lead or contribute to special projects such as process improvements, new disclosure requirements, and merger and acquisition reporting.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What As Manager, Engineering, Git & Gitaly Operations, you'll lead the team responsible for the infrastructure layer underneath Git at GitLab: the open source Git project itself, Gitaly, GitLab's Git storage and remote procedure call layer, and the services that make Git perform at enterprise scale.</p> <p>Git and Gitaly are core to GitLab. If they go sideways in production, they affect everything downstream, including continuous integration, code review, and deployments. This role starts with genuine subject matter expertise in Git technologies and extends to reliable operation across GitLab's deployment models: Self-Managed, GitLab Dedicated, and SaaS.</p> <p>You'll build and develop a team with deep platform expertise and strong operational judgment. You'll partner across engineering groups to shape how Git and Gitaly operations evolve as the platform grows.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Build and lead a team with deep platform expertise in Git and Gitaly, hiring and developing engineers who can operate this infrastructure layer with strong operational judgment.</li> <li>Own production reliability for Git and Gitaly each deployment model so operational practices stay coherent rather than fragmenting into separate playbooks.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems fundamentals, including consistency, replication, and failure domains, to Gitaly's storage and replication model.</li> <li>Own elastic storage and compute strategy for Git repository data, including capacity planning, autoscaling, and consumption-based provisioning for GitLab's largest self-managed and SaaS customers.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Familiarity with GitLab's product and deployment models, and how Git and Gitaly support repository operations across self-managed, dedicated, and SaaS environments.</li> <li>Hands-on subject matter expertise in Git internals, including how the protocol, object model, and storage layer behave under load and at scale, not only familiarity with Git usage.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems fundamentals, including consistency, replication, failure handling, and horizontal scalability.</li> <li>Experience running production infrastructure across multiple deployment models, such as self-managed, dedicated or single-tenant, and multi-tenant SaaS, or a credible path from adjacent experience to it.</li> <li>Experience with elastic storage and compute, and consumption-based system design for variable, unpredictable load.</li> <li>People management experience, ideally leading site reliability engineering-style or platform operations teams.</li> <li>Direct experience with Gitaly, libgit2, JGit, or another Git implementation's internals is advantageous.</li> <li>Experience operating cloud-agnostic infrastructure across multiple hyperscalers or on-premises environments is advantageous.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Git & Gitaly Operations team owns the Git infrastructure layer that powers GitLab and works at the intersection of Git internals, distributed systems, storage, and production operations.</p> <p>We expect the Git & Gitaly Operations team to go deep on one of GitLab's most critical platforms. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Manager, Engineering, Nonlinear Productivity (Friction Elimination & Solutions), you’ll help GitLab break the linear relationship between headcount and engineering output. In this role, you’ll oversee the initiative’s forward-scanning work, reviewing GitLab’s software development lifecycle and code-generation workflows to spot recurring friction, test durable fixes, and identify internal solutions that could become customer-facing products.</p> <p>You’ll report to the Senior Manager or Director, Nonlinear Productivity and work at the intersection of engineering, developer productivity, AI-assisted development, and product. You’ll build a data-backed view of where technical interventions can have the highest leverage, test solutions through prototypes, drive validated fixes into internal adoption, and help build the case for productizing the strongest outcomes.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Survey GitLab’s internal software development lifecycle and code-generation workflows to identify structural friction early, and build a data-backed view of where technical interventions will have the highest leverage.</li> <li>Evaluate build, buy, and adapt options for each opportunity, including emerging agentic and AI tooling, with a clear view of cost, risk, and durability.</li> <li>Stand up prototypes and review architecture directly to test whether a proposed fix moves a target metric and represents a durable solution before GitLab makes broader engineering investment.</li> <li>Hire and manage a small, high-caliber team, or operate as a hands-on working manager, with a focus on talent density over headcount.</li> <li>Drive validated fixes from prototype to internal adoption by partnering with affected teams so solutions are relied on, used, and maintained.</li> <li>Build the technical and business case for productizing internal fixes that prove durable, in partnership with product.</li> <li>Document reusable learnings so successful internal fixes don’t remain tribal knowledge.</li> <li>Report impact through changes in key metrics and progress on turning internal fixes into products, including a clear account of what didn’t work.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Ability to use GitLab.</li> <li>A track record of identifying and shipping technical fixes for developer productivity, continuous integration and continuous delivery, or platform friction, including problems you found before they were assigned.</li> <li>Comfort operating with high ambiguity and no existing backlog, building the roadmap rather than executing one handed down.</li> <li>People management experience, including in a small-team or working-manager capacity.</li> <li>Technical depth to evaluate and prototype solutions directly, not only direct others toward them.</li> <li>Product judgment to assess whether an internal tool could hold up for paying customers.</li> <li>Familiarity with agentic or AI-assisted development tooling.</li> <li>Experience moving an internal tool toward an external, customer-facing product is advantageous.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Nonlinear Productivity team improves how GitLab engineers, and increasingly agents, build, review, and ship code. We test and scale durable technical fixes that improve our internal engineering output. </p> <h2><strong>Career ladder</strong></h2> <p>In this role, you can progress to Senior Manager, Nonlinear Productivity, with an expanded mandate across the full set of team metrics we use to track improvement.</p> <p>Additional details about our process can be found on our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/">hiring page</a>.</p> <p><br><br></p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. You will be an individual contributor, reporting to the Senior Director, SOX PMO Leader within the Chief Accounting Officer's organization, you'll directly support the Senior Manager, IT SOX PMO in strengthening GitLab's IT SOX program, preparing new and changing processes and systems for SOX requirements, and advancing automation in a high-growth technology environment. You'll combine strategic guidance with hands-on execution by improving current processes, assessing emerging technologies for SOX impact, and applying practical, scalable control practices.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Serve as an IT SOX subject matter expert for ITGCs and ITACs, providing guidance and supporting compliance with SOX requirements.</li> <li>Partner with the business SOX Program Management Office (PMO) to assess SOX readiness for new or changing systems and business processes, and support the annual IT SOX risk assessment.</li> <li>Maintain and improve control documentation, including flowcharts, risk and control matrices, and control inventories.</li> <li>Facilitate IT control walkthroughs and coordinate the remediation of control deficiencies.</li> <li>Coordinate with internal and external auditors throughout the SOX audit cycle, clearly presenting positions and supporting appropriate conclusions.</li> <li>Review System and Organization Controls (SOC) reports and oversee the key report testing program with contractor support, performing hands-on testing when needed.</li> <li>Build cross-functional relationships, including a close partnership with Internal Audit on SOX testing execution.</li> <li>Identify opportunities for control automation, monitor emerging risks and regulatory changes, including those related to artificial intelligence (AI), and help prepare reports and presentation materials on SOX compliance status.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, accounting, or a related field.</li> <li>IT audit and SOX compliance experience, including deep knowledge of ITGCs, ITACs, and control frameworks such as Control Objectives for Information and Related Technologies (COBIT) and the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) framework.</li> <li>A current Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), or Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) certification.</li> <li>Experience working in the software as a service (SaaS) industry.</li> <li>Proficiency with governance, risk, and compliance tools; experience with AuditBoard is a plus.</li> <li>Professional judgment, critical thinking, and clear written and verbal communication skills, including persuasion, influence, and conflict resolution.</li> <li>A practical and creative approach to complex problems, audit findings, and recommendations, with familiarity using AI tools to improve compliance processes.</li> <li>Ability to collaborate effectively across US Pacific and Eastern time zones.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The SOX PMO team is a second-line function within GitLab's Chief Accounting Officer organization. It owns and manages the enterprise SOX compliance program across risk assessment, control design, documentation, and coordination with external auditors, while Internal Audit operates as the independent third-line function responsible for SOX testing. analytical solutions and tools.</li> <li>Own the quality, structure, and usability of sales data in partnership with central data teams, ensuring consistency across Snowflake, dbt models, and other data sources where relevant.</li> <li>Manage stakeholder expectations and project timelines, prioritizing requests and communicating trade-offs and outcomes in a clear, structured way.</li> processes, documentation, and standards so the team can work more efficiently and reuse high-impact analytical assets.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Background
