title: Senior AI Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As an Senior AI Engineer at GitLab, you'll help build the foundation for GitLab's transformation into an AI-first company. Reporting to the Director, Enterprise AI, you'll be a hands-on technical leader responsible for delivering internal AI-powered solutions that drive measurable business outcomes.</p> <p>Building fast matters, but it's not enough on its own. This role starts with understanding the real problem: mapping how work moves across teams, tools, and handoffs, identifying the true constraint, and validating whether AI is the right solution before you begin development. From there, you'll take ownership from discovery through deployment, combining strong engineering skills with systems thinking and business understanding.</p> <p>Your initial focus will span Sales, Marketing, and Customer Support, where you will embed AI solutions into key systems and workflows. This role offers the opportunity to shape how GitLab team members work, improve flow across the organization, and help advance our mission in a remote, asynchronous, and values-driven environment.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Diagnose business problems before building solutions. Map workflows, identify constraints, and confirm whether AI is the right intervention. Be prepared to say "this doesn't need AI" when that's the honest answer.</li> <li>Own AI initiatives end-to-end, from stakeholder discovery and technical design through implementation, deployment, and iteration.</li> <li>Design, develop, and ship AI-powered solutions quickly, delivering working prototypes in days, not months, with a focus on practical outcomes and measurable business value.</li> <li>Improve organizational flow by building solutions that reduce bottlenecks, shorten lead times, and increase throughput. Measure success using flow metrics alongside adoption and ROI.</li> <li>Integrate AI capabilities into existing systems and workflows using APIs, orchestration tools, and modern AI platforms, including GitLab Duo Agent Platform, where appropriate. The right tool wins, whether that's custom code, a platform, or a well-crafted prompt.</li> <li>Be Customer Zero: leverage and showcase GitLab's AI offerings wherever possible, feeding real-world usage insights back to R&D.</li> <li>Partner closely with stakeholders across functions to understand the real constraints. Ask the right questions, bridge technical and non-technical perspectives, and align on outcomes before jumping to solutions.</li> <li>Define and track success through business metrics, flow metrics, and feedback loops that make performance visible and actionable.</li> <li>Contribute to technical direction by evaluating tools, documenting patterns, and creating reusable foundations that help the team scale its impact.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>A Technologist at Heart - </strong>Genuinely invested in technology, the foundational and the cutting-edge in equal measure. You're as energised by a well-designed API integration as you are by the latest foundation model release. You reach for the simplest solution that solves the problem well, rather than forcing new technology when proven approaches would do. AI is a powerful part of your toolkit, but it sits on top of solid engineering fundamentals, not in place of them.</li> <li><strong>Competent, Confident Coding Skills - </strong>You can build working solutions end-to-end, write clean and maintainable code, and debug effectively. Whether your skills were honed in a traditional engineering role, through building automations, or shipping side projects, what matters is that you can deliver production-quality work independently.</li> <li><strong>AI</strong><strong> & LLM </strong><strong>Technical Depth - </strong>Strong proficiency in at least one modern scripting language (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar) and a solid understanding of REST APIs, GraphQL, and integration patterns. Deep, practical experience with modern AI technologies, specifically: Prompt engineering as a core discipline: designing effective system prompts, managing context windows, structuring multi-turn interactions, evaluating output quality, and iterating systematically on prompt design.</li> <li><strong>Model selection and cost-performance trade-offs: </strong>understanding when a smaller fine-tuned model outperforms a general-purpose large one, when RAG is the right architecture versus expanding the context window, and how to make principled decisions about capability versus cost.</li> <li><strong>Agentic architecture patterns: </strong>tool use, multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop designs, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and production-grade reliability patterns.Practical fluency across the LLM ecosystem: hands-on experience with models from Anthropic, OpenAI, open-source alternatives, and the judgment to know which to reach for and when.</li> <li><strong>AI Safety & Risk Awareness - </strong>You think critically about how the solutions you build could be exploited, misused, or produce unintended consequences. You know how to design appropriate guardrails (input validation, output filtering, access controls, prompt injection defences, and data leakage prevention) and you treat these as first-class engineering concerns.</li> <li><strong>Systems Thinking & Diagnostic Rigour - </strong>The ability to look at a complex process and see the constraint. Comfortable mapping how work flows end-to-end, identifying bottlenecks, and tracing problems to root causes before proposing solutions. You instinctively ask "what's actually blocking flow here?" before asking "what model should I use?"</li> <li><strong>Business System Expertise - </strong>Familiarity with the landscape of enterprise business systems, CRM (Salesforce), marketing automation (Marketo), support platforms (Zendesk), integration and orchestration tools (Workato), AI platforms (Relevance AI), and enterprise search and knowledge tools (Glean). You don't need deep experience with all of these, but to understand what they do, how they fit together, and be willing to build with and across them. A strong understanding of enterprise data models and workflows is essential.</li> <li><strong>Broad Functional Understanding - </strong>Ability to have meaningful conversations with stakeholders across diverse domains and quickly understand their unique needs.</li> <li><strong>End-to-End Ownership - </strong>Track record of owning complex initiatives from discovery through delivery. Comfortable operating with ambiguity and driving to measurable outcomes independently.</li> <li><strong>Product Mindset - </strong>Ability to scope MVPs, prioritise ruthlessly, and deliver iteratively. In addition, consider adoption, user experience, and business outcomes.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Preferred requirements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with GitLab platform and CI/CD workflows</li> <li>Background in consulting, solutions engineering, or customer-facing technical roles</li> <li>Familiarity with value stream mapping, flow metrics, or Theory of Constraints thinking</li> <li>Experience with low-code/no-code orchestration tools (n8n, Make, Workato) alongside custom development</li> <li>Previous startup or high-growth company experience</li> <li>Experience mentoring or leading technical projects with junior engineers</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>You will join the Enterprise Technology & AI team. We're the backbone of the organisation, driving transformation in how GitLab team members make decisions, operate at scale, and deliver results for our customers.</p> <p>We believe the best AI solutions start with understanding the system, not the technology. We value people who think in constraints and flow, who build with conviction, and who never stop learning. We work in an all-remote, asynchronous setting, guided by GitLab's values of collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. title: Senior Assigned Support Engineer (EMEA)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As an Assigned Support Engineer, you’ll be a trusted technical advisor to GitLab’s largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, helping them avoid operational disruption and get the most from GitLab. You’ll combine deep Linux systems expertise, GitLab and CI/CD knowledge, and a proactive support mindset to understand each customer’s environment, anticipate and prevent issues, and solve complex technical and business challenges. In a typical week, you might be prioritizing strategic blockers with customer stakeholders, partnering with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales to drive defect resolution and influence the roadmap, or diving into code, logs, and tools like strace to troubleshoot performance issues. Your impact in the first year will be measured by customer trust, reduced critical incidents, and clear, reusable support content that empowers customers and GitLab teams alike.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Provide technical support to our largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, ensuring their GitLab environments remain stable and performant.</li> <li value="2">Troubleshoot and resolve complex, critical, and sensitive support issues using tools like Zendesk, logs, and Linux utilities such as strace, through email and video conferencing.</li> <li value="3">Build strong, proactive relationships with key customer stakeholders, helping them prioritize and address their most important technical blockers.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate with <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/product/">Product</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/development/">Development</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure/">Infrastructure</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-success/">Customer Success</a>, and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/sales/">Sales</a> teams to drive bug fixes, influence feature development, and help shape product goals and roadmap.</li> <li value="5">Act as a technical expert on GitLab and CI/CD implementations, advising customers on how incidents and service interruptions impact their workflows and how to mitigate them.</li> <li value="6">Create and improve support content, including documentation and knowledge articles, to help customers and GitLab team members resolve issues more efficiently.</li> <li value="7">Partner closely with Support Engineering team members through <a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-pairing/?_gl=1%2a1vj7usl%2a_ga%2aMTYyOTI0OTAxNC4xNjc4NzIwMDg0%2a_ga_ENFH3X7M5Y%2aMTY4NDgzNDU0OC4xMTAuMS4xNjg0ODM2NDM3LjAuMC4w">pairing sessions</a> and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/#support-stable-counterpart">stable counterpart</a> relationships to share knowledge and solve problems together.</li> <li value="8">Contribute to team growth by participating in hiring processes, including reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Background managing complex, customer facing support cases end to end, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution.</li> <li value="2">Advanced troubleshooting skills with the ability to investigate ambiguous, multi-layered technical issues and identify root causes across applications, infrastructure, and integrations.</li> <li value="3">Strong Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent), including performance analysis and low-level debugging tools.</li> <li value="4">Practical experience with GitLab and continuous integration / continuous delivery (CI/CD), including how different deployment models and outages affect customers.</li> <li value="5">Ability to write and maintain clear, reusable support content such as knowledge articles, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides.</li> <li value="6">Proficiency with scripting languages (such as Ruby or Bash) and familiarity with model-view-controller (MVC) frameworks, preferably Ruby on Rails.</li> <li value="7">Effective communication skills for explaining complex technical topics to audiences with varying technical backgrounds and for building rapport with customer stakeholders.</li> <li value="8">Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless platforms, with openness to applying transferable skills from related domains.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Support team is a fully distributed, global group across the AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions, focused on helping customers get the most from GitLab by troubleshooting complex issues and digging into code and logs to understand why something is not working as expected. As an Assigned Support Engineer, you’ll be part of our broader Support Engineering organization, working closely with other Support Engineers through regular pairing sessions, 1:1s, coffee chats, and Slack conversations to stay connected while collaborating asynchronously across time zones. title: Senior Backend Engineer, AI Engineering: Chat
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Duo Chat team, focused on Chat Engine, you'll build the core AI capabilities behind GitLab Duo Chat, the natural-language and agentic interface to the GitLab DevSecOps platform. Much of your work will involve building flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry, the Python framework built on LangGraph within our Duo Workflow Service that powers agentic chat, and integrating them with the GitLab Rails monolith.</p> <p>You'll own complex backend features from start to finish across both services. You'll integrate large language models and orchestrate multi-agent flows so customers can work faster and more securely across the software development lifecycle. This work sits where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy, and reliability, performance, and answer quality directly shape the customer experience.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Design and build flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry using Python and LangGraph within the Duo Workflow Service. These reusable building blocks power agentic Duo Chat and, increasingly, other AI features across GitLab.</li> <li>Develop, ship, and maintain backend features for GitLab Duo Chat across the Python Duo Workflow Service and the GitLab Rails monolith in a secure, well-tested, and performant way.</li> <li>Integrate new generative AI models, providers, tools, and multi-agent orchestration patterns into Duo Chat to expand its capabilities and improve answer quality.</li> <li>Design, implement, and review GraphQL and Representational State Transfer (REST) application programming interfaces (APIs) and related monolith logic, including chat entry points, permissions, and foundational-flow registration. Keep contracts with frontend clients and host systems reliable and clear.</li> <li>Improve debugging, observability, and test coverage using pytest, RSpec, and related frameworks; track and improve latency, error rates, and test coverage so AI-powered chat workflows stay reliable at scale.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product, User Experience (UX), frontend, and AI specialists to refine requirements and deliver high-quality improvements through iteration.</li> <li>Document standards, patterns, and learnings with other engineers, raising the bar for safe AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.</li> <li>Participate in Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and strengthen resiliency.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Significant experience building and maintaining production Python backends, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous or long-running workloads.</li> <li>Practical experience designing and shipping AI-powered, agentic backend features, including large language model integration, tool or function calling, and multi-agent orchestration. You use sound judgment about large language model limitations and safe use in production.</li> <li>Working proficiency in Ruby on Rails, or a strong willingness to learn it. Duo Chat integrates deeply with the GitLab monolith for chat entry points, GraphQL, permissions, and flow registration, and most of GitLab's codebase is written in Ruby.</li> <li>Proficiency designing or extending REST or GraphQL APIs with attention to scalability, maintainability, and backward compatibility.</li> <li>Strong Structured Query Language (SQL) skills and familiarity with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, including efficient queries and data modeling.</li> <li>Ability to find, diagnose, and prevent performance and reliability problems at scale.</li> <li>Experience solving technical problems of high scope and complexity and advocating for quality, security, and performance improvements across your team.</li> <li>Openness to learning and collaborating in an async-first, distributed team, applying transferable skills from related technologies or domains. Hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph or LangChain is a strong plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We're part of GitLab's AI Engineering organization and own the AI-powered chat experience embedded across the GitLab platform. Chat Engine is the backend-focused team within the Duo Chat group.</p> <p>We're backend, frontend, and AI specialists working asynchronously across time zones, using issues, merge requests, and documentation as our main collaboration tools. Our focus is to expand generative and agentic AI capabilities, improve the performance and reliability of chat workflows, and strengthen the debugging and testing foundations that let us run AI features safely at scale.</p> <p>For more on how we work, see the <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/ai/duo-chat/">team handbook</a> page.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. kits with a single, unified solution that teams can rely on.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Guide the design, implementation, and evolution of a unified data collection platform using Golang, Kubernetes, ClickHouse, and NATS, with success measured by reliability, performance, and adoption across GitLab teams.</li> <li value="2">Improve the emission, transit, and quality of instrumentation data across the system, with success measured by data quality, data integrity, and usage billing accuracy.</li> <li value="3">Provide technical guidance for usage billing and instrumentation systems during working hours, with success measured by timely incident handling, effective root cause analysis, and reliable service restoration.</li> <li value="4">Work across the value="5">Make technical choices that balance ease of use for product teams with reliability and correctness for data consumers, with success measured by platform usability and reliable downstream data.</li> <li value="6">Mentor other engineers through code reviews, design discussions, and clear technical documentation, with success measured by stronger code quality, faster technical alignment, and more maintainable systems.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Significant experience working with platform or infrastructure systems in production environments.</li> <li value="2">Strong proficiency in the Go programming language, with experience building and maintaining production services.</li> <li value="3">Strong backend development experience, with the ability to design and deliver scalable, reliable systems serving internal and external customers.</li> <li value="4">Experience guiding technical design and making tradeoffs across system reliability, performance at scale, data quality, and observability.</li> <li value="5">Experience working across team boundaries with product teams, data consumers, and other internal stakeholders.</li> <li value="6">Familiarity with cloud native technologies and open source development practices.</li> <li value="7">A track record of mentoring other engineers and helping teams make clear, well-documented technical choices.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Analytics Instrumentation team operates at the intersection of Product, Analytics, and customer-facing teams, providing data collection infrastructure that serves engineering teams across GitLab. We're a distributed team of generalist engineers who tackle complex problems spanning the GitLab codebase, JavaScript, Go, and Python satellite services, data pipelines, and AI tool integration. We collaborate transparently across teams, deliver measurable results through efficient iteration, and build inclusive solutions that respect user privacy. Our work enables data-informed choices and planning across the organization. engineers</strong> on the team in agentic-workflow standards, prompt discipline, evaluation methodology, and the principles of human-AI collaboration in platform readiness</li> <li><strong>Contribute to technical documentation and architectural decision records</strong> that document the Platform Readiness team's technical evolution and rationale for key design choices</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <h3>Required Experience & Skills</h3> <ul> <li><strong>5+ years of software engineering experience</strong> with at least 2+ years in backend, platform, or developer-facing tooling</li> <li><strong>Strong proficiency in TypeScript/Node, Python, or Golang</strong> (Ruby a plus)</li> <li><strong>Experience shipping developer-facing tooling</strong> where the primary user is another engineer</li> <li><strong>Understanding of GitLab-style development workflows</strong> (issues, epics, merge requests, CI/CD, code review) as first-class artifacts that automation can read and reason about</li> <li><strong>Ability to work in cross-functional environments</strong> across multiple platform teams</li> <li><strong>Experience with structured content systems, schemas, or validation tooling</strong></li> </ul> <h3>Highly Valued Experience</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Experience with AI/agentic systems</strong> (DAP, ADK, LangGraph, or similar) OR demonstrated ability to reason rigorously about the boundary between what AI should decide and what humans must own</li> <li><strong>Experience integrating with LLM APIs</strong> and reasoning about cost, latency, evaluation, and failure modes</li> <li><strong>Background in developer experience or platform engineering</strong></li> <li><strong>Experience with governance patterns</strong> for shared standards and cross-org decision-making</li> <li><strong>Open source contribution history</strong> in platform, developer experience, or AI infrastructure</li> <li><strong>PostgreSQL or other relational database experience</strong> at scale</li> </ul> <h3>What Makes You Stand Out (Strong Plus)</h3> <ul> <li>You've <strong>shipped agentic workflows in production</strong> and dealt with the operational complexities of AI-driven automation</li> <li>You have <strong>experience designing schema-driven content systems</strong> with non-engineer authors and evolving them as requirements change</li> <li>You've <strong>built developer platform teams at scale</strong> and understand the dynamics of enabling other engineers</li> <li>You have <strong>observability and monitoring experience for AI systems</strong>, including evaluation metrics, cost tracking, and failure analysis</li> <li>You can <strong>explain complex concepts</strong> (agentic workflows, platform readiness, governance) clearly to platform teams, feature teams, product managers, and executives</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Platform Readiness team is part of GitLab Developer Experience, building internal You'll be a key member of the Legal leadership team and a trusted executive partner to the CFO, People organization, and broader E-Group on corporate governance, securities, equity, compliance, ethics, and M&A matters. You'll set the tone for how corporate legal operates as a strategic business enabler, accountable for the programs, judgment, and infrastructure that let GitLab operate as a scaled public company with rigor and speed.</p> <p>This role spans corporate governance, securities compliance, compliance, ethics, equity plan administration, executive compensation, and M&A, building and leading a team of corporate attorneys and paralegals as GitLab's corporate and compliance legal needs continue to grow. This is a role for a seasoned legal leader who has operated inside a public company, who knows what great governance looks like at scale, and who is ready to shape the corporate legal function for a company operating at the intersection of DevSecOps, AI, and enterprise SaaS.</p> <p><strong> </strong></p> <p><strong>What You'll Do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Define and execute the long-term strategy for GitLab's corporate and compliance legal function, aligning legal priorities with the company's public company obligations, governance standards, and growth trajectory</li> <li>Serve as a primary legal executive partner to the CFO, People leadership, and E-Group, advising on corporate governance, securities matters, equity strategy, executive compensation, and M&A at the highest levels of complexity and materiality</li> <li>Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of corporate attorneys and paralegals, fostering a high-performance, async-first culture as the function scales</li> <li>Advise on, draft, and maintain templates, policies, and processes for corporate law matters, including securities filings, governance documentation, equity plan administration, executive compensation, and M&A transactions</li> <li>Own GitLab's ongoing SEC reporting and disclosure obligations, working closely with Finance, Accounting, and external auditors on legal issues relevant to accounting treatment and public company disclosure</li> <li>Lead legal support for equity plan administration, partnering with Stock Administration, People, and Total Rewards on plan design, grant practices, and compliance</li> <li>Monitor and analyze changes in corporate and securities law, assess legal risk, and propose creative, practical solutions that account for GitLab's culture, brand, and business priorities</li> <li>Anticipate legal issues and risks tied to GitLab's continued scale, building the processes and systems needed to minimize potential impact</li> <li>Champion AI-enabled legal workflows within the corporate legal team, driving adoption of tools that make governance, disclosure, and contract review faster and more consistent</li> <li>Manage outside counsel relationships across corporate, securities, and M&A matters, ensuring efficient and effective use of external resources</li> <li>Serve as a senior voice on cross-functional initiatives involving Legal, Finance, People, and Investor Relations, influencing decisions that shape how GitLab operates as a public company</li> </ul> <p><strong> </strong></p> <p><strong>What You'll Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years of combined law firm and in-house legal experience, with substantial tenure leading corporate legal matters at a multinational, publicly traded technology company</li> <li>J.D. or U.S. law degree equivalent with bar admission in good standing in at least one U.S. state</li> <li>In-house public company experience with strong working knowledge of the '33 Act and '34 Act, and demonstrated experience managing SEC reporting and disclosure obligations</li> <li>Proven success partnering across business units, including Finance, Stock Administration, Accounting, People, and Marketing, to resolve complex business and risk management issues while weighing non-legal variables such as culture, brand, communications, government relations, tax, and insurance</li> <li>Experience advising executives and the board on corporate governance, securities, equity compensation, and M&A matters</li> <li>Demonstrated fluency in applying AI tools to legal workflows, with a track record of driving adoption across a team rather than just individual use</li> <li>Practical, creative problem-solving approach that emphasizes addressing business needs while protecting GitLab's interests</li> <li>Proactive, dynamic, and results-driven leader with strong attention to detail and familiarity working across time zones and cultures</li> <li>Outstanding interpersonal and executive communication skills, with the ability to interface effectively across all business functions with a responsive, service-oriented attitude</li> <li>Sound, practical business judgment and demonstrated ability to lead in a fully remote, asynchronous environment</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>About the Team</strong></p> <p>The Corporate and Compliance Legal team partners with Finance, People, and the broader E-Group to support GitLab's obligations as a public company. You'll join and lead a globally distributed team that works asynchronously and closely with internal stakeholders and outside counsel on governance, securities compliance, equity administration, and M&A. Our focus includes maintaining rigorous public company processes, keeping pace with evolving securities and corporate law requirements, and strengthening enablement through clear documentation, training, and AI-supported workflows.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. growth.</li> <li>Support AI self-serve initiatives within the Field through certified data sets, coordination with Ent Data on semantic layers and metric definitions.</li> <li>Lead a team building insights via AI tooling and solutions along with legacy BI solutions.</li> <li>Own the analytics roadmap across sales, customer success, and professional services to improve sales productivity, retention, services utilization, and revenue performance.</li> <li>Develop and support forecasting, pipeline, capacity, and predictive models to improve forecast accuracy, conversion, velocity, resource allocation, and revenue planning.</li> <li>Build customer lifecycle analytics for onboarding, product adoption, engagement, churn risk, expansion, NRR, and GRR to improve customer outcomes.</li> <li>Provide strategic leadership on the metrics, insights, and data necessary to help the GTM functions migrate to a consumption-based business model.</li> <li>Create executive artifacts to be used on recurring basis, integrated reporting, attribution models, and strategic analyses that connect acquisition, post-sale, and services performance.</li> <li>Partner with executive leaders and teams across Revenue Operations, Marketing, Finance, Product, Professional Services, and Enterprise Data & Analytics to turn business questions into clear recommendations.</li> <li>Establish data governance and reporting frameworks that improve data quality and provide reliable insights for executive, board, and external reporting.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience leading analytics teams and developing team members in sales, customer, revenue operations, business intelligence, or consulting environments.</li> business models.</li> <li>Ability to develop strategic analytics roadmaps, translate complex data into clear insights, and influence executive-level decisions.</li> <li>Experience with customer success analytics, including health scoring, churn prediction, NRR and GRR analysis, segmentation, and expansion analytics.</li> <li>Experience with sales and professional services analytics, including forecasting, revenue planning, utilization, project profitability, and services-led growth metrics.</li> <li>Ability to work with large, complex datasets to develop analytical frameworks that inform resource allocation, capacity planning, and customer outcomes.</li> <li>Advanced proficiency with AI tools (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini), Business Intelligence tools (Tableau, Hex, Omni), Structured Query Language (SQL), data modeling, statistical analysis, and predictive modeling for customer analytics.</li> <li>Familiarity with customer data platforms, product analytics tools such as Gainsight or Pendo, services management systems, and other business intelligence platforms is a plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Revenue Analytics team are full-stack title: Senior Engineering Manager, Non-Linear Productivity

description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal"><span style="font-size: 14pt;"><strong>About the role</strong></span></p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Senior Engineering Managers at GitLab own outcomes for a defined engineering domain, build and grow the team that delivers them, and are trusted to operate with significant autonomy against a clear mandate.</p> <p>This Senior Engineering Manager role focuses on driving non-linear productivity by building and leading a small, hand-picked team of engineers who find and fix the highest-leverage friction points in GitLab's own SDLC. Rather than incremental team management, this is a 0 to 1 team-building mandate. You will personally recruit 4 exceptional engineers, define how they work, and drive them through a root-cause, shift-left approach to engineering productivity, measured in system-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency), not story points or activity.</p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">You will act as a bridge between the pilot squad, engineering managers whose teams are affected by friction points, and leadership, ensuring the team's fixes deliver durable, measurable value before any of it is proposed as a permanent function.</p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">This role reports to a VP-level engineering leader.</p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal"><span style="font-size: 14pt;"><strong>What you'll do</strong></span></p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Vision & Strategy</p> <ul> <li>Define and continuously refine the operating model for the non-linear productivity pilot: what "friction" means, how it's diagnosed, and how fixes are prioritized against the three system-level metrics.</li> <li>Identify and prioritize non-linear productivity opportunities (step-change fixes rather than incremental gains) across the SDLC, including flaky tests, review latency, pipeline reliability, tooling gaps, and context loss for both human and agentic contributors.</li> <li>Translate an intentionally broad, ambiguous mandate ("find the friction, fix it at the root") into a concrete, time-boxed roadmap with defined milestones for a 3-month pilot window.</li> </ul> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Team Building & Leadership</p> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Personally source, evaluate, and select 4 exceptional engineers for the pilot squad. You own this hiring bar directly rather than delegating it to a pipeline.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Negotiate allocation models (100% vs. partial/dual-hat) with each engineer's current EM, balancing team commitments against the pilot's needs.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Set the technical direction and working norms for a small, fast-moving team: how work is scoped, how decisions get made, and how progress gets reported.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Mentor the engineers on this team in root-cause diagnosis and shift-left thinking, raising the bar for rigor versus reaching for the nearest patch.</li> </ul> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Deep Technical Exploration & Experimentation</p> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Lead hands-on investigation to instrument and baseline the three top-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency) so the org has an honest starting point before any fix is proposed.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Diagnose the highest-leverage friction points dragging each metric down, and validate hypotheses with real data before committing team time to a fix.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Design and implement fixes that compound, including shift-left quality changes, tooling investment, and better context and interfaces for both humans and agents, rather than one-off patches.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Stay hands-on enough to review architecture, dig into pipeline internals, and unblock the team on hard technical problems directly.</li> </ul> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Internal Adoption & Non-Linear Productivity</p> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Own a small set of high-impact friction areas as pathfinders, driving each from diagnosis through fix to measurable metric movement.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Work directly with affected engineering teams to ensure fixes are trusted, adopted, and don't quietly get reverted or worked around.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Track and report metric movement honestly, including when a bet didn't pay off.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Capture and codify reusable patterns and playbooks so that fixes validated by this team can be adopted org-wide with minimal friction.</li> </ul> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Operations, Risk & Enablement</p> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Set a cadence for reporting impact back to EM peers and leadership, framed around metric movement rather than activity.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Ensure the pilot's fixes degrade gracefully and don't introduce new reliability risk into CI/CD systems that other teams depend on.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Help define what "graduation" from pilot to permanent function looks like, and build the case (or the honest counter-case) based on results.</li> </ul> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal"><span style="font-size: 14pt;"><strong>What you'll bring</strong></span></p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">General</p> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Track record leading small, high-autonomy engineering teams, ideally in developer productivity, CI/CD, platform, or infrastructure reliability, measured on system-level outcomes rather than feature delivery.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Deep comfort with CI/CD and build systems. You understand why pipelines flake, why they're slow, and what actually moves success-rate and latency numbers versus what just feels like progress.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Demonstrated root-cause instinct and a bar for talent over headcount: you'd rather run understaffed than fill a seat with someone good-enough.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Comfort operating under metrics-driven accountability, including publicly baselining a number and reporting honestly against it.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Strong executive-level communication. This pilot has direct visibility to engineering leadership.</li> </ul> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Nice to have</p> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Experience with agentic or AI-assisted development workflows, and a view on where human/agent friction shows up differently than pure human friction.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Prior experience running a defined-window pilot or 0 to 1 initiative with explicit success criteria.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Familiarity with GitLab's own CI/CD internals, or equivalent depth on another large-scale build/test system.</li> </ul><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An overview of this role</strong></p> <h4> </h4> <p>The Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager is responsible for strategizing, executing, and optimizing data-driven lifecycle communications for GitLab’s product-led and self-service audiences. This role collaborates with Product Growth, SMB Sales, Marketing Ops, Data, Product Marketing, Campaigns, and regional teams to plan and prioritize programs that engage free, trial, self-managed, and self-service users and guide them toward activation, conversion, and revenue growth. They will focus on leveraging audience data, product signals, cross-team collaboration, and continuous testing to improve lifecycle performance and scale effective programs.</p> <h4> </h4> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Create, monitor, and improve automated lifecycle journeys and triggers with static and dynamic content to help educate, activate, and convert product-led and self-service users.</li> <li>Lead the creation and implementation of lifecycle campaigns from conception through execution, including planning, copywriting, segmentation, testing, QA, launch, and performance optimization.</li> <li>Develop programs that support free-to-paid, trial-to-paid, self-managed-to-paid, and sales-assisted conversion paths.</li> <li>Lead lifecycle campaigns from planning through launch, including copywriting, segmentation, testing, QA, execution, and performance analysis.</li> <li>Partner with Product Growth, SMB Sales, Marketing Ops, Data, Product Marketing, Campaigns, and regional teams to align on audience strategy, messaging, handoffs, and measurement.</li> <li>Use performance insights to identify gaps, recommend improvements, and continuously optimize lifecycle programs.</li> <li>Act as an email marketing SME, helping the team apply best practices across creative, segmentation, personalization, deliverability, testing, and execution.</li> </ul> <h4> </h4> <p>What You’ll Bring</p> <ul> <li>5+ years of lifecycle, email, CRM, or growth marketing experience, preferably at a B2B SaaS or product-led growth company.</li> <li>Strong experience building and optimizing nurture programs, automated journeys, and trigger-based lifecycle campaigns.</li> <li>Experience supporting onboarding, activation, engagement, conversion, or self-service revenue programs.</li> <li>Expertise in Marketo or Iterable, including audience segmentation, smart lists, email templates, dynamic content, testing, and QA.</li> <li>Strong email marketing expertise, including copywriting, editing, personalization, experimentation, and performance optimization.</li> <li>Experience using campaign, funnel, or product engagement data to identify opportunities and improve results.</li> <li>Strong cross-functional coordination skills, with experience partnering across Growth, Sales, Marketing Ops, Data, Product Marketing, and regional teams.</li> <li>High attention to detail across audience logic, segmentation, QA, personalization, localization, and reporting.</li> <li>Working knowledge of HTML and CSS for email design or troubleshooting.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Lifecycle Marketing team creates personalized, scalable programs to engage prospects, customers, and users at every stage of their journey. Our goal is to showcase GitLab's value, empower effective product use, and drive meaningful connections through touchpoints like sales meetings, events, and webinars. We own the email channel, one of GitLab's most effective tools for communicating with our diverse audience of developers, IT professionals, and business leaders.</p> <p>We operate at the intersection of data, creativity, and user experience, with team members dedicated to nurturing prospects, converting self-service users, and expanding relationships with existing customers. title: Senior Manager, Product Management: Agentic Software Delivery
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Manager of Product Management, you will lead one of GitLab's most strategic product portfolios: Agentic Software Delivery, spanning Continuous Integration, Artifact Management, Continuous Deployment, and Observability. This is a people leadership role. You will guide senior, domain-expert product managers and define how these connected areas evolve as AI agents take on more of the execution work in building, testing, shipping, and monitoring software.</p> <p>Today these are treated as separate stages with a human making the call at each handoff. That model is changing. As agents write more of the code and take on more of the pipeline and deployment work, the real product challenge shifts to how much of that judgment the system can make on its own, safely, and how quickly a production signal turns into a fix without waiting on a human to notice it first. You will own the product vision for that shift and for how customers move from today's manual checkpoints toward more agent-driven ones, at whatever pace fits their risk tolerance.</p> <p>In your first year, you will set direction across this portfolio, strengthen alignment with engineering and go to market partners, and give GitLab customers a clearer path for managing software delivery at scale. This role suits a product leader who can connect technical strategy, commercial outcomes, and team development while influencing across a broad part of GitLab's platform.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Lead a team of senior and principal product managers across Continuous Integration, Artifact Management, Continuous Deployment, and Observability, providing strategic direction, coaching, and support.</li> <li>Define the product strategy and long-term vision for GitLab's Agentic Software Delivery portfolio, with a clear point of view on how AI is changing software delivery workflows.</li> <li>Connect portfolio decisions across build, package, deploy, and monitor experiences so the customer journey is coherent across the platform.</li> <li>Collaborate with engineering leadership on platform investments, architectural direction, and trade-offs across the portfolio.</li> <li>Drive pricing, packaging, and go-to-market alignment with product marketing, sales, pricing, customer success, and solutions engineering to support commercial growth across the portfolio.</li> <li>Use customer insight and product data, including usage telemetry, retention signals, and adoption patterns, to guide roadmap prioritization and improve product adoption and retention.</li> <li>Champion migration and adoption paths that help existing customers move from current workflows to more advanced CI/CD and AI-enabled delivery models, increasing adoption across the platform.</li> <li>Model AI-native product management by using AI tools for discovery, synthesis, prototyping, roadmap exploration, and product concept development, while guiding the team to do the same.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience leading product managers in a people leadership role, including setting direction, mentoring senior talent, and maintaining a high bar for product management.</li> <li>Hands-on product management experience in one or more relevant domains such as CI/CD pipelines, artifact or package management, release management, or observability.</li> <li>Ability to own a broad portfolio across multiple product areas and align teams around a shared product vision and execution model.</li> <li>Technical fluency to work credibly with engineers and architects on topics such as pipeline design, artifact workflows, deployment strategies, and observability signals like logs, metrics, and traces.</li> <li>Experience working with technical customers in developer tools, DevOps, or software delivery environments where engineers and engineering leaders are primary users.</li> <li>Comfort with pricing and packaging decisions for technical products, including working across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.</li> <li>Strong communication and influence skills, with the ability to align executives, cross-functional partners, and customers around a clear strategy.</li> <li>Practical use of AI tools in product management workflows, along with a thoughtful view on how AI and agentic workflows are changing software delivery. We welcome candidates whose experience may come from different but transferable product and leadership paths.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We bring together senior product leaders across GitLab’s software delivery platform and work closely with engineering, design, and go-to-market partners to ensure customers experience these capabilities as one connected system. We help customers manage today’s delivery complexity while shaping how AI-powered and AI-native workflows influence the next generation of software delivery. As part of GitLab’s all-remote organization, we collaborate asynchronously across regions with a strong focus on transparency, written communication, and clear decision-making.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups">underrepresented groups</a> are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. methods, including regression, forecasting, hypothesis testing, and survival analysis, to identify meaningful trends in people data.</li> <li>Serve as a subject matter expert for surveys at GitLab, including survey design consultation, platform configuration, implementation, factor analysis, text analysis, trend identification, and results analysis.</li> <li>Own people analytics intake and office hours, helping stakeholders frame business questions, triage requests, and get value from existing reporting solutions.</li> <li>Create and maintain clear documentation for data definitions, business rules, analytical methods, and reporting solutions.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience in analytics, preferably within People Analytics, Recruiting Analytics, or a closely related function.</li> <li>Experience developing reports and dashboards with business intelligence tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or similar platforms.</li> develop and deliver presentations for senior and executive audiences.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to produce well-organized reference materials.</li> <li>Experience with Workday reporting and data extraction, people systems such as Greenhouse or Culture Amp, or AI experimentation and automation in analytics workflows is helpful but not required.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The People Technology & Analytics Job Family owns the technology and reporting solutions at GitLab. Know when AI is the right solution versus a traditional approach.</li> <li>Ship and iterate – Break complex AI experiences into releases that fit GitLab's cadence without sacrificing quality. Define success criteria upfront, use evidence to drive decisions, and work closely with PM, Engineering, and Technical Writing to get things over the line.</li> <li>Set the craft bar – Set quality standards through strong visual and interaction design, and provide constructive feedback that raises the level of work around you. </li> <li>Define strategic direction – Bring validated user evidence and a strong point of view to roadmap discussions before direction is set. Contribute AI-specific patterns to Pajamas Design System that others can build on, and share knowledge that raises the design quality of AI experiences across GitLab.</li> <li>Mentor and grow – Guide other designers in developing their skills, participate in hiring by interviewing candidates and evaluating portfolios, and share what you know generously.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;">What You'll Bring</span></h2> <ul> <li>A strong portfolio showing how you think and iterate, not just what shipped, ideally including AI/ML products, agentic workflows, or natural language interfaces where user control, transparency, and trust were key considerations.</li> <li>Experience designing for AI workflows. You care deeply about the details of interaction and visual design, and help others raise their standards too.</li> <li>Experience conducting research and translating findings into clear, well-reasoned design decisions.</li> <li>Proven ability to work iteratively in agile product development, balancing speed with quality and making smart tradeoffs without losing sight of the longer-term vision.</li> <li>Experience designing in complex enterprise contexts, with working knowledge of Git, HTML/CSS, accessibility best practices, and design systems.</li> <li>Excellent communication skills. You can simplify complexity, articulate design rationale clearly, and bring people along through your process.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;">About the Team</span></h2> <p>The AI Product Design team is part of GitLab's broader UX organization, focused exclusively on creating exceptional experiences for AI-powered features across our DevSecOps platform. performance and take action.</li> <li>Partner with operational and data teams to define requirements for stakeholders and engagement data models, shaping how data is collected, structured, and made programs.</li> <li>Serve as a subject matter expert in sales analytics by sharing best practices, documenting logic and methodologies, and providing guidance to help partners and other analysts use data to make better decisions.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience in analytics roles focused on pre-sales motions and SaaS, including analyzing customer engagement, adoption, and health across the customer lifecycle.</li> <li>Background combining data from multiple customer and go-to-market systems to create a unified view of pre-sales and Partner engagements and outcomes.</li> <li>Proficiency writing complex SQL queries with joins, aggregations, common table expressions, and conditional logic to support reporting and in-depth analysis.</li> <li>Drive analysis of pipeline, pre-sales engagements, trial success rates, and other sales metrics using SQL and Python to uncover trends, risks, and opportunities.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with Sales, Field Operations / RevOps, Finance, and Customer Success partners to translate business needs into scalable analytical solutions and tools.</li> <li>Partner with teammates to define the quality, structure, and usability of sales data in partnership with central data teams, ensuring consistency across Snowflake, dbt models, and other data sources where relevant.</li> <li>Ability to and methods, including generative AI and experimentation techniques, and to applying transferable skills from related analytics or data roles.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> The team works asynchronously across time zones, using GitLab and our data stack to collaborate on projects, share context, and maintain transparency. Current priorities include strengthening our sales analytics foundation, deepening our use of business intelligence tools like Tableau, and building repeatable analytics that help stakeholders quickly understand performance and identify opportunities to improve results.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. preference for cost-effective and AI-native alternatives to legacy suites.</li> <li>Experience developing account segmentation and messaging based on solution-oriented or "jobs to be done" strategic programs from the ground up.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the Team</strong></h3> <p>You'll join our account-based marketing (ABM) team within Growth Marketing, the group responsible for building targeted programs for the accounts that matter most to our growth. You'll partner closely with teams across the business to bring account-focused programs to life.</p> <p>This is a staff-level individual contributor role reporting to our Senior Director of Digital Marketing, with real autonomy to run your own initiatives and shape how the team's programs are built and measured.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. You'll play a central role in how we integrate AI into CI/CD workflows. Your work will impact performance, reliability, and usability for people running millions of CI jobs, from small teams to the largest enterprises.</p> <p>AI is a top priority in the year ahead. In this role, you'll go beyond using AI tools and help define how we design, build, and iterate on AI-assisted and agentic CI experiences. You'll set standards for what good looks like across our AI agent portfolio, including how we measure success, how we instrument behavior in production, and how we account for large language model limitations. You'll also help responsibly integrate GitLab's Duo Agent Platform into CI workflows at scale, on a foundation that's fast, reliable, secure, and observable.</p> <p>We have ambitious goals for <a href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/20586"><em>Agentic CI</em> in FY27</a>. As a Staff Engineer, you will:</p> <ul> <li>Partner with Engineering, Product, and UX leadership to pressure-test our priorities: where we can move faster, where we're missing data, and where there's whitespace to innovate. Part of this includes learning and growing with the Engineering team you will collaborate closely with.</li> <li>Define what success looks like across our agent portfolio and make sure we're tracking against it — not just shipping, but learning.</li> <li>Bring a sharp eye to the competitive landscape, helping us understand what it takes to keep GitLab CI best-in-class in an increasingly agentic world.</li> <li>Examples of <strong><em>Agentic CI</em></strong> work we have planned for the upcoming year:</li> <ul> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/20443"><strong>AI Pipeline Builder</strong></a>, the foundational CI agent that auto-creates pipelines for new projects and serves as the launchpad for onboarding new CI users.</li> <li>Automate the <a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/588753"><strong>Fix a Failing Pipeline</strong> flow</a> at scale – from dogfooding on internal GitLab projects through to safe, controlled rollout for customers, solving real infrastructure and scalability challenges.</li> <li>Build the <a href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/20904">instrumentation and observability</a> layer that makes agentic CI trustworthy — trigger volume dashboards, retry rates, cost safeguards — so we can measure what's working, catch what isn't, and iterate with confidence.</li> <li>Harden the CI pipeline execution infrastructure that these agents depend on: database access patterns, background processing, and job orchestration built to handle the additional load that AI-driven automation introduces at enterprise scale.</li> </ul> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Shape and scale GitLab CI backend infrastructure to improve performance, reliability, and usability for users running jobs at high volume.</li> <li>Design and implement AI-powered features for Agentic CI, including agents, agentic flows, and LLM-backed tooling that integrates with GitLab's Duo Agent Platform.</li> <li>Define what success looks like for AI in CI before you build, including baselines, measurable outcomes, and clear signals that help the team learn and iterate.</li> <li>Build the instrumentation and observability needed to make AI-assisted CI trustworthy in production, including feature behavior metrics, dashboards, and safeguards.</li> <li>Own and drive measurable performance improvements across CI systems (for example, database access patterns, background processing, and job orchestration) by forming hypotheses, running experiments, and validating results with data.</li> <li>Write secure, well-tested, maintainable Ruby on Rails code in a large monolith, improving existing features while reducing technical debt and operational risk.</li> <li>Lead cross-functional technical work with Product, UX, and Infrastructure, influencing architecture and execution across the Verify stage.</li> <li>Share standards, patterns, and learnings with other engineers, raising the bar for responsible AI integration and evidence-driven engineering across CI.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Advanced proficiency with Ruby and Ruby on Rails, with experience building and maintaining reliable backend services in a large codebase.</li> <li>Strong PostgreSQL skills, including data modeling, query tuning, and scaling large tables through proactive performance investigation and remediation.</li> <li>Hands-on experience building, running, and debugging high-traffic production systems, ideally in CI, workflow orchestration, or adjacent infrastructure-heavy domains.</li> <li>Practical experience designing and shipping AI-powered backend features and integrations, including sound judgment about large language model limitations and responsible use in production.</li> <li>A data-driven approach to engineering: defining hypotheses, establishing baseline metrics, instrumenting changes, and measuring outcomes against clear success criteria.</li> <li>Familiarity with observability patterns and tools (metrics, logging, tracing) to diagnose issues, improve reliability, and guide iteration.</li> <li>Strong backend architecture and delivery practices, including secure design, well-tested code, and strategies for safe rollouts and zero-downtime changes.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication skills, including writing technical proposals and documentation, and collaborating effectively in a remote, asynchronous, cross-functional environment.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Verify stage focuses on collaboration, iteration, and helping GitLab users run fast, reliable, and scalable Continuous Integration (CI) pipelines for projects of all sizes, from small teams to large enterprises. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact.
